title: Why I'm writing every day
body:
I'm going to write something here every day.

Some days I won't have anything to say. I'll write anyway.

But I've noticed that I consume all day. Feeds, podcasts, product pages, other people's opinions on other people's opinions.

And I make almost nothing with it.

So this is the deal I'm making with myself. For every day I take in, I put one thing back out. A page. Sometimes a good one. Mostly not.

I'm calling it Dynamic Consumption, because consuming isn't the problem.

Standing still while you do it is.
highlight: Standing still while you do it is.

title: The second cup
body:
The first cup of coffee is for waking up.

The second cup is for thinking.

Most people skip the second one. They drink the first on the way to something and never sit down with the second.

I don't mean caffeine.

I mean the twenty minutes after you're awake and before anyone needs you. It's the most valuable time you own and most of us hand it to our phones.

Tomorrow, try the second cup. No screen.

See what shows up.
highlight: The second cup is for thinking.

title: Buy the expensive one, once
body:
My grandfather owned one good coat.

He wore it for thirty years. It got better.

I've owned maybe forty coats. None of them got better. Most got thrown out.

I used to think buying cheap was the sensible choice. It isn't. It's just the choice with the smaller number on the receipt.

Buy the expensive one, once.

Then wear it until it's yours.

title: Taste is a muscle
body:
People talk about taste like it's something you're born with.

I don't buy it.

Taste is just a lot of looking, a lot of comparing, and a lot of being wrong in private.

You see a thousand chairs and one day you can tell a good chair from a bad one in half a second. You can't explain it. But you know.

That isn't magic. It's reps.

If you want better taste, look at more things. Carefully. And ask yourself why you like the ones you like.

title: Nobody reads the second paragraph
body:
Nobody reads the second paragraph.

So say the thing in the first one.

(If you're reading this, you're the exception. Thank you.)
highlight: So say the thing in the first one.

title: Hotels are stories you can sleep in
body:
The best hotels don't sell rooms.

Anyone can sell a room. A bed, a shower, a kettle that's slightly too small.

The best hotels sell a version of you. The you that reads a book in the bar at 4pm. The you that doesn't check email. The you that was always meant to wear a robe.

You check out and you miss that person more than the room.

That's the whole trick. And it works on brands that have nothing to do with hotels, too.

Don't sell the thing. Sell who people get to be around it.
highlight: Sell who people get to be around it.

title: Make it worse
body:
When I get stuck on something I try to make it worse.

Deliberately. The ugliest version. The dumbest headline. The most obvious idea.

It takes the pressure off. You can't fail at making something bad.

And about half the time, somewhere in the bad version, there's a line that's actually good. Something I'd never have found while I was trying to be clever.

Perfect is a locked door.

Worse is a window someone left open.
highlight: Worse is a window someone left open.

title: Things I didn't buy this week
body:
A watch I saw in an ad three times.

A second pair of white trainers, almost identical to the first.

A course on how to be more productive.

A book I'll definitely read, eventually, next to the other twelve I'll definitely read eventually.

I'm not against buying things. I love buying things. That's sort of the problem.

The practice isn't saying no to everything. It's noticing the gap between wanting something and needing it, and standing in that gap for a day or two.

Most wants don't survive forty-eight hours.
highlight: Most wants don't survive forty-eight hours.

title: Your inputs become your outputs
body:
You are what you eat.

You also write what you read, design what you look at, and say what you hear.

If everything going in is the same feed everyone else is scrolling, don't be surprised when everything coming out looks like everyone else's.

Read old books. Look at old buildings. Talk to old people.

Change the inputs. The outputs follow.
highlight: Change the inputs. The outputs follow.

title: Sunday
body:
No big idea today.

It rained. I walked anyway. Got soaked. Felt great about it.

Sometimes the page is just the page.
highlight: Sometimes the page is just the page.

title: The brand is the boring stuff
body:
Everyone wants to work on the logo.

Nobody wants to work on the email you get when your parcel is late.

But the email is the brand. So is the box. So is the way someone answers the phone. So is the refund.

The logo is what people see once.

The boring stuff is what they remember.
highlight: The boring stuff is what they remember.

title: Finish things
body:
I have a folder on my laptop called ideas.

It is a graveyard.

Half-written essays. Brand names with no brand. A business plan that's mostly a nice font.

Here's what I've worked out. An unfinished thing has no value. None. It can't be sold, shared, criticised or improved.

A finished thing, even a mediocre one, can be all four.

So finish it. Ship the small version. Then make it better in public.

title: Say it out loud
body:
If you're writing something and you're not sure it's any good, read it out loud.

Your ear is a better editor than your eye.

Your eye forgives clunky sentences. Your mouth trips over them.

If you wouldn't say it to a friend across a table, don't write it.

(I read this one out loud three times. It used to be much longer.)
highlight: Your ear is a better editor than your eye.

title: Consume like a maker
body:
There are two ways to watch a film.

You can watch it like an audience. Sit back. Let it happen to you.

Or you can watch it like a director. Why is the camera there? Why did that scene end early? Why does that song make the moment work?

Same film. Completely different experience.

You can do this with everything. A menu. A shop window. A good sentence.

That's all I mean by dynamic consumption. Same films. Same shops. Eyes open.

See you tomorrow.
